entries.title: Power: meaning, quantity symbol, unit, and distinction from energy and power factor

entries.title: Power factor: meaning, notation, dimensionless nature, and distinction from power
entries.whyHeld: Narrowed from 3 unresolved dimensions to 1: DISTINCTION and QUANTITY_SYMBOL are now resolved (see below), but UNIT_SYMBOL (power factor's formal dimensionless/no-unit attestation) has no permitted-class (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY / PROFESSIONAL_BODY / AUTHORITATIVE_TECHNICAL_REFERENCE) source that explicitly states it -- IEC's own power-factor entry (IEV 131-11-46) is silent on unit, unlike sibling entries; only a general BIPM 'unit one' principle applies via disclosed inference, and LibreTexts' explicit statement is not a permitted class for this SYMBOL_OR_CONVENTION-mode dimension.
entries.resolution: DISTINCTION resolved via LibreTexts explicit statement (see EQCT-LP-05 route); QUANTITY_SYMBOL resolved via IEC Electropedia IEV 131-11-46 (symbol lambda, correcting the prior "cos phi"/"p.f." assumption). UNIT_SYMBOL remains genuinely unresolved after a real, bounded, permitted-class-respecting search (IEC Electropedia, BIPM SI Brochure, targeted web search for IEC/ISO/IEEE/NIST statements) -- not fabricated closed. [Narrow correction pass, Stage D] The genuinely final gap (power factor's UNIT_SYMBOL/dimensionless attestation) is now closed: IEC 60050's general "factor" entry (IEV 112-03-04) states in its own Note 2 that "a factor is a quantity of dimension one", explicitly naming power factor among its examples -- a permitted-class (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY) source stating the fact directly, not an inference. EQCT-LP-07 is now READY.

entries.title: Fleming's right-hand (generator) rule
entries.whyHeld: No permitted-class source was found and read in text form stating the exact thumb=motion/first-finger=field/second-finger=current mapping specifically for the RIGHT-hand GENERATOR rule (not the left-hand motor rule, not the unrelated grip rule). Two prior dedicated re-sourcing attempts confirmed a genuine citation trail (Wikipedia -> Hughes, "Electrical & Electronic Technology", 12th ed., p.145) but could not render/read that edition's page through any available tool.
entries.resolution: [Section E, third narrow correction pass] Located and directly read the equivalent passage in a different, earlier edition of the same published textbook: Edward Hughes (revised by Hiley, Brown and McKenzie Smith), "Hughes Electrical and Electronic Technology", 10th edition, Pearson Education Limited, 2008, ISBN 978-0-13-206011-0, Chapter 6, section 6.9(a) "Fleming's right-hand rule", printed page 141 -- accessed via a FlipHTML5-hosted page-image scan (disclosed only as the retrieval route), and confirmed genuine by its own header, page number and section sequence. The passage states in text: "If the first finger of the right hand is pointed in the direction of the magnetic flux ... and if the thumb is pointed in the direction of motion of the conductor relative to the magnetic field, then the second finger, held at right angles to both the thumb and the first finger, represents the direction of the e.m.f."

entries.title: The simple AC generator: parts and how they work together
entries.whyHeld: Narrowed from 2 unresolved requirements (single-loop-alternator-generator-parts, coil) to 1 (coil only); slip-rings and brushes were already VERIFIED.
entries.resolution: single-loop-alternator-generator-parts is now VERIFIED: DOE Fundamentals Handbook Module ES-07 "Basic AC Theory" (a different module of the same already-accepted handbook family) explicitly and repeatedly describes a genuinely single loop ("a conductor, or loop of wire" / "a conductor loop"), fully labelled with field, slip rings and brushes. The coil's own standardised schematic-SYMBOL geometry remains genuinely unresolved: IEC 60617 is login-gated, and a real IEEE Std 315-1975/ANSI Y32.2-1975 lead (Section 6.2, naming inductor/coil/winding symbols) was found but its only located copy is truncated before the relevant page. [Narrow correction pass, Stage C re-adjudication] The coil requirement was genuinely conflated with a different (AC6.2) question -- a generic IEC 60617 circuit-schematic symbol for an inductor, EDA-LP-16's territory. The qualification's own manifest (acquisitionTargetId ACQ-123) confirms this requirement belongs to AC5.4, whose genuine intended mastery (recognising the coil/winding as a labelled part of a simple AC generator diagram) is directly answered by the already-registered DOE Fundamentals Handbook evidence. All four required dimensions are now VERIFIED; EMI-LP-17 is now READY.

entries.title: Recognising the schematic symbols for Unit 202 components
entries.whyHeld: This is a breadth requirement over all 15 AC6.2 component families. 13 of 15 already have real, directly-read symbol geometry from IEEE Std 315-1975/ANSI Y32.2-1975 (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY, disclosed foreword-claimed IEC-117/predecessor compatibility). 2 of 15 (LED, inverter) have no dedicated named symbol in that 1975 standard -- only a general symbol plus an inserted letter code, which is genuinely how that standard represents them, not a sourcing failure. Separately, the CURRENT IEC 60617 database's own free preview confirms 6 relevant ID/name pairs (including LED as S01919) but not their artwork/geometry or Standard/Obsolete status, both of which sit behind a paid login not accessed in this pass.
entries.resolution: [Section G, third narrow correction pass -- RE-ATTEMPTED, STILL BLOCKED at that time] Freshly re-checked the official current IEC 60617 database via both webstore.iec.ch and library.iec.ch, and searched for a products.iec.ch individual-record route for S00684 (LDR)/S00896 (inverter)/S01919 (LED): all confirmed the same subscription-gated picture, no free geometry or per-entry status access exists. One genuine correction surfaced: BS EN 60617 is WITHDRAWN, so IEC 60617 itself (not a separate BS EN edition) is the current standard. [Section 4/H, this pass -- RESOLVED, per an explicit Product Architect decision] Rather than waiting on the paywalled current-IEC-60617 geometry, this pass ran one bounded acquisition pass on the SAME already-registered 1975 IEEE Std 315/ANSI Y32.2 standard, personally re-opening it as page images (not from memory or a prior snippet). This closed both remaining breadth gaps genuinely, not by relaxing the bar: LED via item 8.5.4.2 'Photoemissive type' (page 56) plus item 11.1.1/NOTE 11.1.1B's explicit 'LED' letter-code association (page 63); inverter via item 16.1.1's own NOTE 16.1C (page 74), which positively confirms the standard's stated policy is a labelled general block precisely when no dedicated symbol exists elsewhere in the standard -- i.e. a directly-evidenced, standard-sanctioned absence of a symbol, not merely a failure to find one. Per the Product Architect's decision, the inverter is taught/assessed only as a clearly labelled DC-to-AC functional block, never as a claimed standard component symbol; the current-IEC-60617-currency caveat remains disclosed (see evidenceReadinessNote) but does not block READY, consistent with how it never blocked the other 13 (now 14) families. No longer the sole core release blocker -- 0 core release blockers remain.
